root_causes.root_cause: LLM audit judge (Opus) non-determinism: all 3 docs have byte-identical extraction between Run 11 and Run 12 (same node counts, char counts, tree structure), but the Opus judge applied different subjective scrutiny. The stored gate verdicts from deterministic classify_verdict (helpers.py:1285) are unchanged -- cabinet_resolution returns PASS (43 nodes, depth 3, max_leaf_ratio well under 0.30), uae_numbers stored MARGINAL (flat_mixed with 748 chars). The audit scorecard 'Verdict' column is the LLM judge verdict, not the stored gate verdict (confirmed by audit line 7: 'stored vs audit verdicts diverge'). RFC-028 D6 already fixed one instance of this pattern (image markers in hierarchical docs) by adding prompt guidance to .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md lines 34-42. The same calibration gap now manifests for two new dimensions: (a) table-header malformation scrutiny (cabinet_resolution: judge now flags malformed multi-row headers it previously tolerated), (b) chart-content-loss severity (uae_numbers: judge escalates from MARGINAL to FAIL for the same 748-char artifact with zero enrichments).
root_causes.code_path: .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md (Judge Verdict guidance section) -> Opus model subjective scoring
root_causes.suggested_fix: Extend the Judge Verdict guidance in .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md with two additional calibration rules: (1) For docs where stored gate verdict is PASS and metrics are byte-identical to the prior run, the judge MUST NOT downgrade unless it can cite a specific content-quality defect not present in the prior run's finding (prevents re-scoring drift on stable artifacts). (2) For flat/chart-heavy docs with low char counts (<1000 chars) and zero enrichments, anchor the severity to MARGINAL (not FAIL) when the extraction layer itself has not regressed -- the missing enrichment is a known pipeline gap, not a per-run regression. This follows the same pattern as RFC-028 D6's fix for image markers.
